I've been farming this land for 40 years in Quzhou. The North China Plain doesn't forgive mistakes, but it rewards those who understand the soil and the seasons. With only two of us in the household and 15 mu to manage, I need to be efficient.

**My thinking:**

My main system is wheat-maize rotation on about 10 mu — that's the backbone. Wheat goes in October, comes out in June, then maize immediately follows on the same ground until early October. I've done this hundreds of times. I'll keep 5 mu for cotton; prices have been uncertain but I know how to grow it and it gives the household cash when grain prices disappoint.

For wheat, I'll use an improved variety like Jimai 22 — it does well in our soils and handles the spring drought. Three irrigations: winter freeze water, jointing, and grain fill. My soil here is moderately fertile so I won't overdo the nitrogen — 16 kg pure N per mu is enough with proper timing.

For maize, I direct-seed hybrid seed (郑单958 or similar) immediately after wheat harvest. No-tillage saves time and moisture. I'll top-dress nitrogen at V6 and again at tasseling. Two irrigations should be enough with the well if summer rains cooperate.

Cotton on the 5 mu gets more attention. It's labor-intensive but the household can manage it. I'll plough in spring, transplant with a hybrid Bt variety in early May. Cotton needs more potassium than people think, and I need to stay on top of aphids and spider mites even with Bt — those pests don't care about Bt toxin.
